purpose: Defense-tech behavioral and fit question bank for the behavioral turn of the Anduril Air Defense interview arc.
usage_policy: Select one pillar per session using the active persona's adaptation. Escalate with the pillar's follow_ups only when the candidate's answer leaves that specific gap open, and prefer a probe built from the candidate's own words. Judge every answer on STAR/STARE completeness, first-person ownership, real friction, and organizational impact.

questions.question: How do you think about the moral and ethical responsibility of designing UX for autonomous weapons and counter-drone C2 systems?
resume_and_role_links: Lattice OS autonomous counter-drone command and control

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: What research philosophy would you use to define and test the moral boundaries of UX for autonomous weapons and counter-drone C2 systems without slowing responsible Air Defense delivery?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: When a non-deterministic counter-drone system can act faster than an operator, what ethical constraints must become hard trust, intervention, and verification requirements?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: How would you turn ethical concerns about autonomous weapons UX into product decisions that preserve mission value without becoming an open-ended reason not to ship?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: Where should an Air Defense operator workflow introduce deliberate friction, confirmation, or control handoff so the physical-digital experience preserves meaningful human authority?

follow_ups: Give me a concrete case where you personally declined to optimize something because of the ethical consequence, not the usability consequence.
Who decides when your ethical line becomes a shipping blocker, and what happens when they overrule you?
How do you keep an ethics position from becoming an open-ended veto that engineering learns to route around?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior holds a personal ethical position. Lead/Staff converts it into a written principle, a review gate, or a control requirement the organization must satisfy.

questions.question: Describe your experience working directly with military operators or high-stress domain experts in field conditions. How do you cut through operator bias or bravado to get true operational data?
resume_and_role_links: NASA Lunar Gateway clinical workstation validation
Anduril in-field rapid ethnography and contextual inquiry

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Using your NASA and field-research experience, how would you design rapid ethnography with Air Defense operators that separates genuine operational constraints from recall bias, status signaling, or bravado?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: How would you convert conflicting operator accounts from stressful field conditions into falsifiable system requirements instead of anecdotes engineering cannot implement?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: When field operators demand mutually incompatible changes, how do you identify the highest-value operational truth quickly enough to influence the next release?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: How would you observe an operator's full physical-digital C2 workflow and reconcile what they say with breakdowns visible in posture, reach, attention, and interaction sequence?

follow_ups: Name the moment an operator or domain expert told you something that turned out to be wrong. How did you find out?
What did you change about your protocol after that, and does it still work when you only get one field visit?
How do you earn credibility with an operator who thinks a researcher with a Ph.D. cannot understand their job?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior runs credible field sessions. Lead/Staff builds the elicitation protocol and access model that lets the whole team get truthful operator data.

questions.question: You hold a Ph.D. and have published in academic tracks like ACM CSCW. How do you balance scientific rigor with Anduril's requirement to ship functional tech in months, not years?
resume_and_role_links: ACM CSCW 2026 Principles for Agentic Trust

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Your Ph.D. and CSCW work show rigor; tell me how you would preserve validity while compressing an Air Defense research program into evidence that changes a decision in weeks, not years.
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: What minimum evidence would you require before turning a psychophysics or trust finding into a latency threshold or verification test on a rapidly changing C2 system?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Give me an example of how you have traded methodological completeness for decision speed without making the resulting product recommendation intellectually dishonest.
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: How would you combine fast prototype testing and service-blueprint work with enough rigor to prevent a rushed C2 interaction pattern from becoming an unsafe design standard?

follow_ups: Name the specific methodological compromise you made and the claim you refused to make because of it.
What is the smallest study you have ever run that still changed a real decision?
Where is the line between a fast study and a dishonest one, and have you ever been asked to cross it?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior moves fast on request. Lead/Staff defines the evidentiary tiers the organization uses to decide how much rigor a given decision deserves.

questions.question: Tell me about a time an Engineering Lead or PM strongly resisted your research recommendations or wanted to strip a safety feature for speed. How did you resolve it?

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Tell me about a time you protected the integrity of a research or safety recommendation under executive pressure while still preserving trust and delivery velocity across the team.
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Describe a technical standoff where engineering rejected your Human Factors threshold or safety control. What evidence, trade space, and verification criterion changed the decision?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Tell me about a time a PM wanted to remove a safety or usability control to hit a date. How did you frame the user risk, business cost, and reversible compromise?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: Describe a conflict over an operator-workflow safeguard or physical-digital interaction. How did you keep research, design, product, and engineering aligned without diluting the safety intent?

follow_ups: What exactly did the other person say, and what did you concede?
Did the decision go your way, and what did you do in the case where it did not?
What mechanism did you put in place so that argument never had to be relitigated?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior wins an argument with data. Lead/Staff leaves behind a standard, threshold, or review gate that removes the need for the next argument.

questions.question: Defense tech requires high-intensity field testing and dynamic schedules. How do you stay effective and prevent burnout under high operational friction?
resume_and_role_links: 25-30% travel scenario supplied for interview preparation

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: How would you build a high-performance research culture that can sustain field intensity and dynamic schedules without normalizing burnout or lowering evidence quality?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: During repeated field-test cycles with shifting hardware and software builds, what operating practices keep your judgment and technical handoffs reliable under fatigue?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: How do you protect the highest-value work and communicate capacity when travel, field failures, and release pressure collide in the same week?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: How do you maintain observational quality and collaborative design judgment during intensive field studies where physical conditions, travel, and rapid redesign cycles create fatigue?

follow_ups: Walk me through your heaviest field-testing month. What actually happened to your evidence quality?
Tell me about a week where the intensity degraded your work. What did you change afterward?
How do you protect a team's sustainability without becoming the person who slows the deployment down?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior manages personal capacity. Lead/Staff builds field-rotation, handoff, and quality-control practices that keep a team's evidence reliable under tempo.

questions.question: How do you design a research strategy when hardware/software requirements are completely undefined and the product team is changing direction weekly?
resume_and_role_links: Sling Human Factors strategy across software, hardware, and AI

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: How would you establish a coherent Air Defense research thesis and repository when product direction changes weekly and no stable policy or requirements exist yet?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: When hardware interfaces, autonomy behavior, and software architecture are all moving, how do you create Human Factors hypotheses that can still mature into testable specifications?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: What research do you fund first when the roadmap changes weekly, and how do you prevent discovery work from becoming obsolete before it changes a decision?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: How would you use service blueprints and workflow models as stable artifacts when screens, hardware controls, and operator roles are all still changing?

follow_ups: What did you commit to in your first thirty days on an ambiguous program, and what did you deliberately leave undecided?
How do you tell the difference between productive ambiguity and a team that has no strategy?
What research did you fund that turned out to be obsolete before it landed, and what did that teach you?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior copes with ambiguity. Lead/Staff imposes a research thesis and sequencing plan that gives other functions a stable frame to work against.

questions.question: What is your protocol when leadership or engineering acknowledges your research findings but decides to ship an unsafe or sub-optimal UX anyway?

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: When leaders accept your evidence but choose a riskier design anyway, how do you document uncertainty, define escalation thresholds, and preserve the research function's influence?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: If engineering ships despite a validated Human Factors failure mode, what severity, detectability, verification, and stop-ship criteria govern your response?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: How do you respond when a roadmap owner accepts your data but chooses to ship a sub-optimal or unsafe workflow for schedule or mission reasons?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: If an unsafe interaction survives design review, how do you preserve the evidence in the service blueprint, negotiate mitigations, and keep the operator workflow from silently normalizing the risk?

follow_ups: Give me the actual sequence: who did you go to first, what did you put in writing, and where did you stop?
What severity of consequence moves you from documenting the risk to formally escalating it?
Have you ever escalated and been wrong? What did that cost you with the team?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior voices the concern. Lead/Staff has a pre-agreed escalation and stop-ship threshold that leadership accepted before the incident.

questions.question: Tell me about a research study or interface design of yours that completely failed during testing. What went wrong, and how did you recover?

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Tell me about a study whose assumptions or methods failed. How did you recognize the failure, protect credibility, and turn it into a stronger research direction?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Describe a test where the interface or system behavior invalidated your Human Factors model. What technical evidence forced the course correction?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Tell me about research that failed to answer the roadmap question or arrived too late. How did you recover value and change your operating approach?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: Describe an interaction design that broke under realistic workflow or ergonomic testing. What did you own, redesign, and validate next?

follow_ups: What was your specific error, as opposed to the team's or the constraint's?
How much time and money did the failure cost, and who else absorbed it?
What practice do you now run every time because of that failure?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior recovers a study. Lead/Staff turns the failure into a checklist, review step, or method standard that prevents the class of error team-wide.

questions.question: How do you scale research operations, build shared insight repositories, and mentor junior team members as a Lead/Staff engineer?

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: What operating system would you build for Air Defense research so repositories, standards, mentorship, and research quality scale beyond your own studies?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: How would you make Human Factors insights reusable by systems and ML teams through traceable requirements, failure modes, and verification artifacts while developing junior researchers?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: How would you build research operations that help multiple product teams find prior evidence, understand decision impact, and avoid repeating low-value studies?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: How would you connect shared insights, service blueprints, design patterns, and mentorship so operator-workflow knowledge compounds across Air Defense products?

follow_ups: Name a person you developed and the specific capability they had after working with you that they did not have before.
What standard or artifact of yours is still being used by a team you have left?
How do you shape team culture when you have no direct reports and no formal authority?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior mentors informally. Lead/Staff builds the repository, review ritual, and growth path that raises the whole function's floor.

questions.question: When three different product managers are demanding urgent user research for different Air Defense platforms simultaneously, how do you triage and allocate your time?
resume_and_role_links: Air Defense product and program strategy

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: How would you allocate scarce research capacity across three urgent Air Defense programs while protecting the long-term research agenda and team health?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: How do you rank simultaneous research requests when one affects a safety-critical autonomy threshold, one blocks integration, and one improves operator efficiency?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Three PMs each claim their Air Defense study is urgent. Walk me through the decision framework, ROI evidence, and stakeholder conversation you use to allocate research capacity.
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: How would you triage competing workflow studies across platforms while preserving shared service-blueprint knowledge and avoiding fragmented operator experiences?

follow_ups: Which request do you say no to first, and how do you say it so that PM still brings you the next problem?
What did you stop doing last time to make room for the highest-value work?
How do you tell a PM their question does not need research at all?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior triages their own queue. Lead/Staff publishes the intake and prioritization framework that makes the trade-offs legible to every stakeholder.
